benchmark: UC-RI-005 Obligation Extraction V1 accuracy benchmark
purpose: Reference run for comparing the future Obligation Extraction Engine V2 against V1 on FCA FG24/6.

run.costBasis: Static pricing USD 3 / 15 per million input / output tokens; confirm against the Anthropic Console.

integrity.note: md5 over the stored values in ai_analysis_runs / ai_analysis_citations at recording time. Recompute to detect any change to the benchmark run.

notes: Model produced 21 candidates; normalisation kept 12 claims (the UI findings). Candidates not represented as findings include: corporate opt-out (p.15), AML / POCA Part 7 compliance (p.15), anti-fraud systems and controls (p.13), notifying the customer of the outcome (p.15), payee PSP acting as quickly as practicable (p.16), monitoring delay proportions and support (p.10, p.17), value dating after an inbound delay (p.17).
Citation status VERIFIED means each cited section ID exists in the supplied PDF section catalogue; it is not a semantic check that the page supports the wording.

humanLabels.labelledBy: Agent analysis against stored source quotations; pending compliance reviewer confirmation

classes.guidance_on_requirement: FCA view of how a binding requirement is met
classes.guidance_expectation: FCA expectation ('should', 'we expect'), not itself a rule
classes.scope_or_definition: Scope exclusion, definition or interpretive threshold

findings.note: Permission to delay up to 4 business days, with conditions. The raw candidate labels it binding_requirement.
Notify payer of delay, reason and needed action by end of next business day; tipping-off exception is FCA guidance.
FCA's view of 'no longer than necessary'.
Liability for charges and interest from a Reg 86(2B) delay; p.9 citation is secondary.
Source: 'We also expect PSPs to treat...'. Finding says 'must' — overstates an expectation as a rule. p.3 citation is feedback-statement context.
'PSPs should record...' — record-keeping expectation supporting Consumer Duty monitoring.

Source: 'it is likely that the PSP will need a real-time human interface'. Finding says Consumer Duty 'require[s]' it — overstated. The underlying Consumer Duty support outcome is binding; this specific means is not.

FCA view on force majeure (Reg 96(2)). Not an obligation. Finding inverts the condition: the source concerns cases where making funds available would breach POCA Part 7 / TA 2000 Part 3, not where delaying would.
Payee-initiated card payments out of scope of Reg 86(2A)-(2D).
'We consider... should remain in the payer's account'.
Clarification that Reg 86 does not prevent deterring the payer.

knownV1Defects: materialiseReviewedClaims always throws AI_AUTONOMOUS_ACTION_BLOCKED (approve_change / approve_obligation are permanently blocked), after the review row, review_status, event and notification are already written. No AI materialisation has ever succeeded on staging. UC-RI-005 acceptance is suspended server-side until fixed.

Latent once materialisation is unblocked: materialisation reads candidates[claimIndex] while review and citations use claims[claimIndex]; for this run 11 of 12 indexes point to a different candidate statement.
The connected review form sends empty acceptedClaimIndexes: ACCEPTED materialises every finding; PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED materialises none. No per-finding selection in the UI (API supports it).
bindingNature is not carried on normalised claims; obligation metadata falls back to the misaligned candidate.
grounding.obligationGradeSuitable=false is not enforced before materialisation.
Citation verification is section-ID membership only (no semantic support check).
preservation: Run row is protected from deletion (no delete policy; trigger ri_refuse_ai_analysis_run_delete). A human review changes review_status only, not the stored output or citations, so the checksums above remain valid. Do not supersede or re-run this run; compare V2 output against the labels above.
